<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown mount --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown mount [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
```

## Arguments

`[TARGET]`
: A partition (e.g. /dev/sdb1) or a disk image file.

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

Always read-only, and as you, through the system's own tools: `udisksctl` on Linux (it checks the mount really is read-only), `diskutil` and `hdiutil` on macOS, `Mount-DiskImage` on Windows. It refuses the running system's partitions, locked encrypted volumes, LVM and RAID members, swap and empty partitions. When the system wants an administrator's password, it shows the command to run instead. What it mounted is kept in `mounts.json` in your data folder.

## Examples

```sh
# a partition `backdown volumes` calls mountable
backdown mount /dev/sdb1
# a disk image: attached read-only, and what is on it mounted
backdown mount /media/archive/Images/old-laptop.img
# what BackDown has mounted
backdown mount
```
